Here’s something I’ve noticed: show someone a fact that contradicts what they believe, and nine times out of ten they won’t say “Oh, I was wrong.” They’ll find a reason the fact doesn’t count. I used to think that was just stubbornness, but I’ve come to think it’s something more human than that. Our beliefs aren’t like items on a shelf that we can swap out when a better one comes along; they’re tangled up with who we are, who we hang out with, and what we’re afraid of. Changing one can feel like losing a piece of ourselves. So if you really want to change someone’s mind, don’t start with the argument. Start with respect, and give them room to save face.
